{"id": "44a69be0-382f-45a3-bdaf-e49cc0f4c832", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "I'm thinking through how to restart EC2 instances tagged ssm-skill-test=true using the AWS-RestartEC2Instance automation runbook, targeting instances by tag and tying execution to a CloudWatch alarm that can halt it via rate control.

I'm drafting the CLI command with start-automation-execution, setting max-concurrency and max-errors, and adding alarm-configuration referencing the ssm-skill-test-cpu alarm, noting the automation role will need cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms permission for this to work.

The alarm only halts the automation once triggered -- instances already restarted won't be rolled back, and keeping concurrency at 1 lets the alarm catch issues before the next instance restarts. Since I don't have a tool to actually execute AWS CLI commands, I'll just hand the user the prepared command rather than running it.

"}]}

{"id": "30b29624-9d26-42ea-9e75-f372bc05c13d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's the command. I haven't run it.

```bash
aws ssm start-automation-execution \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --document-name "AWS-RestartEC2Instance" \
  --target-parameter-name InstanceId \
  --targets "Key=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true" \
  --max-concurrency "1" \
  --max-errors "1" \
  --alarm-configuration "IgnorePollAlarmFailure=false,Alarms=[{Name=ssm-skill-test-cpu}]"
```

**What each part does**
- `--target-parameter-name InstanceId` with `--targets "Key=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true"` runs the runbook once for every instance with that tag.
- `--alarm-configuration` attaches the `ssm-skill-test-cpu` alarm. If it goes into ALARM, the automation stops and starts no more restarts.
- `IgnorePollAlarmFailure=false` means the automation also stops if it can't read the alarm state. Set it to `true` if you'd rather it keep going in that case.
- `--max-concurrency "1"` restarts one instance at a time. The alarm is only checked between steps, so a low concurrency means it can halt the rollout before many instances have been restarted. Raise it if you accept restarting more instances before the alarm can take effect.
- `--max-errors "1"` stops the rollout after one failed instance. Adjust this to your tolerance.

**Before you run it**
- The alarm must exist in us-east-1 in the same account.
- If you use an assume role, add `--parameters "AutomationAssumeRole=arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/<role-name>"`. Note that this role needs `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms` for the alarm check to work, as well as the EC2 and SSM permissions the runbook needs.
- A restart is disruptive. Stopping on the alarm only prevents further restarts. It doesn't undo instances that were already restarted.
- To see which instances will be targeted first, run `aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-1 --filters "Name=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true" --query "Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId"`.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
